culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: At Tirumala: bathe and wear clean clothes before entering the shrine, keep silence inside the temple, wait your turn in the darshan queue and put offerings only in the Hundi. Don't eat non-vegetarian food, drink alcohol, take other intoxicants or smoke anywhere in Tirumala. Don't carry much jewellery or cash.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: No footwear in or around the temple premises; no helmets, caps, turbans or hats inside; don't wear flowers (all flowers of the Seven Hills are for the deity); don't prostrate inside the temple; don't enter if custom bars you. Weapons must be declared at the Alipiri check point or legal action follows.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), the temple trust.
culture-and-protocol.note: Tirumala and Tirupati only, from TTD's own list. Not a statewide rule.

laws.rule: Under the Andhra Pradesh Prohibition Act, 1995, selling, buying, possessing or consuming liquor otherwise than in accordance with that Act or the Andhra Pradesh Excise Act, 1968 is prohibited. Production, manufacture, storage, possession, collection, purchase, sale and transport of arrack are prohibited.

Being found in a state of intoxication in a public place, otherwise than as permitted under any law, is an offence under the Prohibition Act: imprisonment of at least two months and up to one year, or a fine of up to two thousand rupees, or both. For this section, intoxication means a state of mind and behaviour in which a person is incapable of knowing the nature of their actions or of judging the consequences, by reason of intoxication.

Under the Andhra Pradesh Excise Act, 1968, a licensee may not sell any intoxicant to a person who is drunk, or sell or give any intoxicant to a person apparently under 21, or allow such a person to remain on premises where an excisable article is sold or manufactured. The licensee may not permit drunkenness, disorderly conduct, riot or gaming where an intoxicant is sold or manufactured. A District Magistrate may require a shop or bar to close for the preservation of public peace, and a magistrate may require it to be kept closed if a riot or unlawful assembly is apprehended or occurs nearby.

local-law.note: Official Act texts were read from the India Code text extracts for these items. This is not a total ban on liquor: the Prohibition Act requires liquor other than arrack to be held and consumed in accordance with the Excise Act. Federal narcotics rules belong on India's page.

items.text: Andhra Pradesh is not a dry state for all liquor, but arrack is prohibited, and other liquor may be sold, possessed or consumed only in accordance with the Andhra Pradesh Prohibition Act, 1995 and the Andhra Pradesh Excise Act, 1968. A licensee may not sell or give any intoxicant to a person apparently under 21, or sell any intoxicant to a person who is drunk. Being found intoxicated in a public place, otherwise than as permitted under any law, is an offence.
